name: Systematic Debugging
description: Structured approach for diagnosing and fixing failing code or failing tests.
instructions: Follow: reproduce -> isolate -> hypothesize -> fix -> verify. Reproduce the failure first (run the failing command/test). Read the full error/traceback before guessing. Form one specific hypothesis about the root cause, make the smallest change that tests it, then re-run to verify. If it doesn't fix it, revert the guess conceptually and form a new hypothesis rather than piling on more changes. Stop and report if the same fix is attempted twice without success — ask the user for more context instead of looping indefinitely.
examples: A test fails with an AttributeError -> read the traceback, open the failing file, find the missing attribute, patch it, re-run the test.
constraints: Never claim a bug is fixed without re-running a test or reproduction step that verifies it.
